objective: Prove, for a connected network of permutation contact with holonomy group H on the witness values W and any commutative ring R with 1 != 0: (1) the basic (level-2) affine relaxation over R is feasible exactly when 1 lies in the ideal of R generated by the sizes of the H-orbits, so over Q every network is accepted, over Z exactly those with coprime orbit sizes, over F_p those with an orbit size prime to p; (2) pinning one witness value makes it refute every value that is not a common fixed point; (3) the level-3 relaxation refutes every impossible network, by an integer certificate valid over every ring, as do path consistency and level-3 Sherali-Adams, while arc consistency and the basic LP refute none. Check each part on declared instances with exact certificates (solutions and refutations verified by substitution). A planning-stage claim that relaxations below the loop's length are fooled was withdrawn before any freeze: three witnesses suffice.
status: Proved by HOLES-COHOMOLOGY-20261019-001C-P001 (prose; certificates built and verified by substitution on 469 networks; three broken certificates rejected; the census agrees). For permutation contact with holonomy group H: the basic two-witness affine relaxation over a ring R accepts exactly when 1 is in the ideal generated by the H-orbit sizes, so Q accepts every impossible network, F_p unless p divides every orbit size, Z exactly when the orbit sizes are coprime; the smallest integer-fooled case has five values with orbits 2 and 3, for example a tie between loops with holonomies (01) and (234). Pinning one witness, or looking at three witnesses at a time (path consistency, level-3 affine over any ring, level-3 Sherali-Adams), refutes every impossible network; arc consistency and the basic LP refute none.
title: Where linear local reasoning fails on a loop
